why: SURVIVOR for the Friday Nordic Soundscapes concert, and its start was an hour early on the row that already carried a verified stamp. The Minnesota Orchestra's own program page sells exactly two performances of this engagement, each with its own BUY button and its own printed time: 'BUY / FRI NOV 13, 8PM CT' and 'BUY / SAT NOV 14, 7PM CT'. So Friday is 8pm, not the 19:00 we published. The per-night pre-concert lobby times corroborate the offset independently - 'Fri Nov 13, 7:15-7:45pm / Sat Nov 14, 6:15-6:45pm', 45 minutes before each printed start. Kept over its duplicate 7a9c7320 because this title names the festival; nothing to carry over from that row. The span to Nov 14 is cleared: two separately ticketed performances with distinct performance ids are not one run (the Wobbleween/Tape B house rule), and Saturday already has its own row 84d5566c, so the span was double-printing Nov 14. End cleared rather than moved: the page prints no end time anywhere, only '~2 hours, including intermission', and CLAUDE.md says never invent an end date. Host note worth keeping: minnesotaorchestra.org returns 403 to plain fetchers, but its block is bot/UA-based and the browser pane reads it fine after the Cloudflare interstitial clears - docs/SOURCE-CHECK.md calls this host unreadable, which is true only of scripted fetches.

duplicate of the Friday Nordic Soundscapes performance kept as c0858631. Same hall, same night, same program, read off the orchestra's calendar under a different title. This row had the RIGHT start time (20:00) and the survivor had the wrong one, which is why the survivor's start is corrected in the same apply rather than this row being kept - the survivor's title names the festival and this one does not.

SURVIVOR for the Friday 11am SPCO premiere. The SPCO's own detail page prints 'Friday, November 13, 2026 - 11:00 AM' and 'Saturday, November 14, 2026 - 7:00 PM' at 'Ordway Concert Hall', each performance with its own Buy Tickets link and a distinct performance id - so there are two performances, the Saturday one already has its own row (473c531d), and the two 11:00 rows are one performance listed twice. The 11:00 start needs no change and is now attested verbatim. Citation moves off content.thespco.org/events/venues/ordway-concert-hall/, a venue index shared by four of our listings and therefore unable to confirm any single one, onto this concert's own page. End cleared, NOT moved to 12:30: the page's only duration string is 'Approximate length 1:30', the organiser's own hedge, printed once on a page advertising two performances, and the music itself sums to 10+26+27 = 63 minutes - so the padding is of unknown composition and 12:30 would be a second guess replacing the first. The stored 13:00 was never attested either. CLAUDE.md: never invent an end date.

duplicate of the Friday 11am SPCO premiere kept as 79b00723. Its title was only the presenter's name, 'Saint Paul Chamber Orchestra', with no event in it, and it cited https://ordway.org/events/ - the venue index, shared by seven of our listings. Its own description gave it away: it described 'the November 13-14 run' rather than one performance, which is the index entry, not a concert.

SURVIVOR for the Gaelynn Lea concert, and the start was wrong on BOTH rows of this pair - they agreed with each other at 19:30 while the Ordway's own page for the show prints 'November 15, 2026' and 'Sunday, 7:00 PM'. A duplicate pair corroborating its own error is the reason a second row is worse than no second row. Two independent reads confirmed the string '7:30' appears nowhere on the page. Citation moves off the shared https://ordway.org/events/ index onto this concert's own page. End cleared: 21:30 was derived by adding the page's '2 hours, 30 minutes with intermission' to the start, which is arithmetic on the page rather than anything it prints. Title deliberately NOT changed - the venue styles it 'It Wasn't Meant to be Perfect: An Evening with Gaelynn Lea and Friends', but our title leads with the artist's name, which is how a reader searches, and changing it would recompute event_key for no reader benefit. NOT carried over from the archived row: its '$25-$65'. The Ordway page prints no dollar amount at all and says 'This event offers flexible choose-your-own pricing to accommodate any budget', so that range is unattested and may have come from an index widget.

duplicate of the Gaelynn Lea concert kept as 9f7a2add. 'Gaelynn Lea Presents' is a presenter line, not the show's title, and it cited the shared https://ordway.org/events/ index. Its price range $25-$65 is deliberately not carried over: the organiser's page prints no dollar figure and describes choose-your-own pricing.

SURVIVOR for the 10am Ordway school performance. The Ordway's own detail page prints the date as 'Nov172026' and lists two performances that day, 'Tuesday, 10:00 AM' and 'Tuesday, 12:00 PM', at 'Ordway Concert Hall', '60 minutes', '$4 per ticket'. The 10:00 start needs no change and is now attested. Citation moves off https://ordway.org/education/school-performances/, the index both rows shared, onto the show's own page, which is what actually carries the date, both times and the price. End cleared: the stored 11:30 is contradicted by the page's '60 minutes' and the alternative 11:00 is that duration added to the start rather than anything printed. NOT FIXABLE HERE: the page prints '$4 per ticket' and this row still says 'See listing', but `price` is not a field lib/corrections.ts accepts - it needs /admin or the next re-find.

REPOINTED, NOT ARCHIVED - and this is a deliberate departure from treating it as a duplicate. At 10:00 it is indistinguishable from c0ad8513, but the organiser's page proves TWO performances on 17 Nov, 'Tuesday, 10:00 AM' and 'Tuesday, 12:00 PM', and we carry only one row for the pair. Archiving this row would be correct about the duplicate and still leave a real, dated, priced performance off the calendar until someone researched it back. The standing rule is that a fuzzy match may confirm but must never destroy, and the burden is on the archive, so this row becomes the midday performance instead: nothing is lost either way, and if it was simply a stale placeholder it is now a listing the venue's own page prints. Its generic title 'Ordway Presents - School Performance (November)' named no event; the new title takes the show's name with a (Midday) suffix, following the house convention already used for 'SPCO: ... (Evening)', which also keeps event_key distinct from the 10:00 row. End cleared for the same reason as its sibling - the page states a 60-minute running time but prints no end.
title: Gravity and Other Myths: Ten Thousand Hours – School Performance (Midday)
